raw_response:
I am 72 years old, and these 12 mu in Quzhou have been my life for 50 years. My back is not what it used to be, and with only two people in my household, I have to be honest about what I can still handle. Wheat and maize are my backbone—I know them like my own children, and I can get machinery to help with harvest and planting. Cotton brings in cash, but picking it by hand at my age is hard, bitter work. So this year, I will put 10 mu into my wheat-maize rotation and keep only 2 mu for cotton. That is enough cotton to give us some money without breaking my body.

The winter wheat went into the ground last October, and now that it is greening up, I will top-dress it with urea and irrigate from my well three times before harvest. Come June, the day after the wheat comes off, I will plant hybrid maize with no-tillage seeding—there is no time to waste between crops, and I am too old to be ploughing in the summer heat. For the cotton, I will rotary-till the 2 mu in late April, plant hybrid seed, and feed it heavy potash because cotton loves potassium. I will irrigate three times and spray four times—cotton pests are greedy, and I do not let them steal my crop. My land is good and my well is reliable, so I expect my usual yields: about 460 kg/mu for wheat, 550 kg/mu for maize, and around 250 kg/mu of seed cotton.
